The preset is very dependent on “Velocity”; the lower the velocity is set, the quieter the guitar sounds. The_Pump_Panel_Reconstruction.serumprese.uploader_description: IMPORTANT READ!!!!! / / The Pump Panel Reconstruction / is a Serum 2 preset that attempts to recreate the “Confusion (Reconstruction Mix)” acid sound from the movie “BLADE” as best as possible. After days of hard work and research, I think I've succeeded—it doesn't get any better than this. But I'm open to being proven wrong—the competition is on. / / (Orig BPM is 136.200) / / "First of all, it's very important not to touch the "Main Volume" control; even the smallest adjustment can change the sound. Do everything in your DAW's Mixing section. The sound is saved to "Clip 1." / The macro knobs labeled "SC-1 --> SC-4" should be positioned either on the far left or far right; the default is left. They change the sound; use them individually, not all at once." / "If needed, you can activate the "Phaser" or "Flanger." I left them off by default, but they sound good." / / The demo track was created with the preset to demonstrate it. / / Download the acapella here: https://presetshare.com/sample/view?id=497 / / What is different from the preset that already exists in "Serum 1"? / / Probably the most important thing is the fact that only a normal bass sound and an LP filter were used. The original BLADE sound, however, was created with a Roland TB-303, and this one doesn't have an LP filter, but rather a ladder filter—an important detail. The ladder filter(New in Serum 2) gives the sound its specific character. For this, I didn't use a normal bass sound wavetable, but rather an original bass sound from a TB-303—also an important detail. An "Electro Harmonix Big Muff" distortion pedal was used in the original bass sound. I got a VST version of the "Electro Harmonix Big Muff" (the free plugin from Nembrini Audio - Big Stuff). I then distorted the sound until it sounded like the original, and then created an "Impulse Response" from this sound. I then loaded this into "Serum 2" and into the "Convolve" effect, which then distorted the bass with the Impulse Response; there's no audible difference compared to the VST plugin. / / I then created an EQ match of the original "Blade Soundtrack" using Fabfilter Pro-Q4 and then recreated it in Serum 2 with the EQs. / / Perhaps this information will help someone. You should look into Impulse Responses; it can be truly magical. / / Enough chatter, have fun!! / / / Impulse Response Creator / Here you can create "impulse responses." It's free and runs in a browser window. / https://29a.ch/impulse-response-creator
